newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TRADE DEFICIT NARROWS TO $29.1 MLN IN FEB.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TRADE DEFICIT NARROWS TO $29.1 MLN IN FEB.

text.p: Romania's trade balance deficit narrowed sharply in February to $29.1 million from $154.2 million the previous month, National Statistics Board (CNS) data showed on Friday.
The two-month trade gap figure was $183.3 million, down from $267.1 million a year before.
"This trend was triggered mainly by a drop in imports," a CNS report said on Friday.

February's imports stood at $635 million, falling 16.1 percent from January, with steep drops in food products. In the first two months of the year imports stood at $1.39 million, down 7.9 percent from the same period of 1996.
Exports remained almost flat at $606.1 million in February, compared to the previous month, but were 3.4 percent down year-on-year.
Textiles and steel showed slight rises in the first two months of the year, when exports amounted to $1.2 billion, or 2.9 percent from the year ago period.
But exports of river and maritime ships and chemical products saw sharp falls, the report said.
The private sector accounted for 55.1 percent of exports and 44.3 percent of imports over January-February when Germany was Romania's top trading partner.
NOTES -- Previous data in brackets. All figures in FOB prices and subject to revisions.
